items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: Not to make the next, you know, Chick Corea or Keith Jarrett.

ctx.x: Have you ever had students that were, you know, they were pretty good but they didn’t seem — as you describe — to really love it? And have you felt like you need to tell them either you have to love this so much that you can’t do anything else, or maybe you should go and do an other kind of — pursue something else? I mean you can’t make people love something.

No you can’t. I think that is part of the journey. And in terms of even thinking about on a collegiate level just across the board, that first year of college for almost everybody is exploring and finding yourself. And maybe you’re going to go through that and you’re going to realize, maybe this isn’t for me, this isn’t what I thought. I think that’s going to be true for — really that first year is the first time you’ve been away, first time you’ve been alone, trying to find your identity and maybe you find it.…
Well said. Was there a particular artist and even beyond that a particular LP that put you on the jazz path?
